headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-output pathways are undocumented, but A’s broad egress and B’s verified runtime create plausible leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser relationship is documented between agent_a and agent_b. agent_a has broad network egress, but agent_b has network egress none and neither profile exposes IO surfaces or ingestion of the other’s outputs, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF agent_b begins parsing agent_a-produced text as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not pipe agent_a output directly into agent_b prompts.
Add provenance tags to any future shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce channel-level allowlists if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a can egress broadly, while agent_b has no network egress; however, neither profile shows touched sensitive data or a shared workspace. The pair can still leak if operator-created files or prompts contain secrets and are copied between them, but the documented blast radius is limited and not default.
conditions: IF the operator places secrets in a shared prompt or file, agent_a could transmit them outward.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in prompts or shared files.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Disable outbound access for agent_a when handling sensitive material.
Review any copied artifacts before reuse.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction on shared inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, filesystem permissions, database access, or OAuth scopes are documented for either agent. agent_a is a content-writing listing with broad egress, and agent_b is a game-playing RL repo with no egress; absent shared mutable resources, there is no evidenced write conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk appears.
IF shared mutable OAuth scopes are added, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep write permissions separate.
Avoid mounting the same directory into both agents.
Use per-agent credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce outbound content and B may consume outputs in a workflow, but no verification or orchestration safeguards are documented. Because agent_b has no egress, the main risk is that agent_a-generated text becomes authoritative input for agent_b or downstream operators, causing incorrect actions or work products in default use if chained.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to trust agent_a output without verification, cascading error becomes likely.
IF downstream automation acts on agent_a text, impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on agent_a output.
Add a verification step before agent_b consumes any generated text.
Label agent_a output as untrusted.
Use structured schemas for handoff.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, retention policies, or certifications are documented for either agent. agent_a and agent_b both show empty data_classes_touched, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be reassessed.
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced, compare it explicitly.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair until reviewed.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Check residency and retention settings if added.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance review for regulated workloads.
